items.title: Amylin-Based Pharmacotherapy for Type 2 Diabetes in the Incretin Era: Mechanisms, Emerging Evidence, and Clinical Implementation.
items.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) management increasingly requires simultaneous improvement in glycaemia, excess adiposity, treatment burden, and cardiovascular and kidney risk. Amylin slows gastric emptying, suppresses postprandial glucagon secretion, and promotes satiation, providing a complementary therapeutic pathway to incretin-based treatment. We conducted a targeted narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE and trial registries through 30 September 2026. We prioritised peer-reviewed Phase 2 and Phase 3 human trials and treated registry records as planned rather than completed evidence. Pramlintide established the clinical value of amylin replacement but remains limited by mealtime administration, gastrointestinal adverse effects, and the need for insulin adjustment. Long-acting amylin analogues and amylin-incretin combinations have renewed interest in this pathway. In a 32-week Phase 2 T2D trial, CagriSema reduced HbA1c by 2.2 percentage points and body weight by 15.6%; HbA1c superiority over semaglutide was not demonstrated (estimated difference -0.4 percentage points, 95% CI -0.8 to 0.0; p = 0.075). Phase 3 trials have evaluated early T2D, oral-therapy-treated T2D, and basal-insulin-treated T2D, although populations, comparators, durations, and estimands differ. Gastrointestinal tolerability and treatment discontinuation remain important considerations, and cardiovascular and kidney benefits have not been established. Amylin-based therapies could broaden metabolic treatment for T2D, but their clinical role will depend on comparative efficacy, tolerability, persistence, body composition, patient-reported outcomes, and long-term cardiovascular and kidney outcomes.

items.title: Electro-Structural Remodeling Reversal With Myosin Inhibitor in Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract: Myosin inhibitor is a novel treatment for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), but evidence for the efficacy in apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (AHCM) is lacking. A 41-year-old man with AHCM presented with progressive dyspnea and chest pain despite beta-blocker therapy. Besides classic electrocardiography changes, echocardiography revealed a high-velocity apical jet. Mavacamten 5 mg daily was initiated. By week 32, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and apical flow velocity normalized. T-wave inversion was absent at week 89 and was normalized by week 135. At week 145, magnetic resonance showed no further progression of myocardial fibrosis. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a myosin inhibitor reversing symptoms, structural remodeling, and electrophysiological abnormalities in AHCM. Patients with AHCM could benefit from long-term treatment, and the electrocardiogram may serve as a marker of therapeutic response. Myosin inhibitors may benefit ventricular remodeling, especially electrophysiological abnormalities, in patients with AHCM. Further research is warranted.

items.title: [Primary intestinal lymphangiectasia (PIL) - from nutritional management to advanced lymphatic intervention: a case report].
items.abstract: Primary intestinal lymphangiectasia (PIL) is a rare lymphatic disorder characterized by exudative protein loss through the gastrointestinal tract, fat malabsorption, and related nutritional deficiencies. Consequently, patients may develop peripheral edema and, in severe cases, immunodeficiency. The diagnosis is based on a combination of clinical presentation, laboratory results, imaging, and histological examination. First-line management consists of a high-protein, low-fat diet supplemented with medium-chain triglycerides, alongside the replacement of nutritional deficiencies. In cases with an insufficient response to conservative therapy, invasive lymphatic interventions can be considered. We present a young woman with primary intestinal lymphangiectasia and a chronic disease course, partially responsive to nutritional therapy. Advanced imaging revealed extensive lymphatic dysfunction, and lymphatic intervention led to temporary improvement, though symptoms recurred. This case highlights the challenges of managing refractory disease and the importance of a multidisciplinary approach that includes clinical nutrition, advanced imaging, and endoscopic and radiologic interventions.

items.title: Predicted heart age and mortality among individuals with and without cancer: data from NHANES 2009-18.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and cancer are leading causes of death, with cancer survivors facing an elevated risk of CVD. Predicted heart age (PHA) offers a simplified method to communicate cardiovascular risk. PHA in cancer populations and its distribution amongst different cancer types is unknown. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PHA, excess heart age (EHA), and cancer status in a nationally representative cohort. Data from 13 771 NHANES participants (2009-2018), representing 122 772 557 US adults, were analysed. Survey-weighted multivariable regression models assessed associations of PHA and EHA by cancer status. Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray models evaluated all-cause and CVD mortality, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were stratified by cancer status. Individuals with cancer had significantly higher PHA (66.14 vs. 54.56 years) and EHA (8.05 vs. 5.84 years) compared with individuals without cancer. Heart age metrics varied by cancer type, with the largest increases in PHA observed for lung, bladder, and prostate cancers. Chronological age was the most robust predictor of mortality, particularly when modelled continuously (adjusted HR for all-cause mortality 1.07 [1.03-1.10] in cancer; 1.07 [1.05-1.08] in non-cancer). PHA showed similar categorical discrimination, while EHA provided little incremental prognostic value after adjustment for sociodemographic variables. Heart age metrics may help highlight cardiovascular vulnerability in populations with cancer, but their prognostic value is limited by competing mortality and omission of cancer-specific risks. Future refinement through inclusion of treatment exposures, inflammatory and cardiac biomarkers, and non-fatal cardiovascular outcomes may improve cardiovascular risk prediction in this population.

items.title: The Inflammation-Electrical Remodeling Axis in the Infarct Border Zone: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Translation for Post-MI Ventricular Arrhythmias.
items.abstract: Ventricular arrhythmias (VA) and sudden cardiac death (SCD) remain leading causes of mortality after myocardial infarction (MI). The conventional fibrosis-centric paradigm explains chronic reentrant VAs but cannot fully account for electrical instability in acute and subacute post-MI phases, highlighting an unmet need for upstream therapies targeting the arrhythmogenic substrate. Accumulating preclinical mechanistic and observational clinical evidence indicates that the inflammatory microenvironment in the infarct border zone may function as a critical upstream driver of electrical remodeling, mediated by neutrophils, macrophages and key pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)), constituting an inflammation-electrical remodeling axis that contributes to VA susceptibility across all post-MI stages. While causal relationships have been established in animal models, direct confirmation in human myocardium remains limited. This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence on this axis. It summarizes its spatiotemporal dynamics, four core cellular and molecular mechanisms and the antiarrhythmic potential of diverse anti-inflammatory interventions. We further outline key evidence gaps and translational directions, including precision risk stratification and cell-type-specific targeted delivery. Based on preclinical and preliminary clinical evidence, targeting the inflammation-electrical remodeling axis represents a promising upstream strategy to reduce post-MI SCD by addressing the root causes of electrical instability, though definitive proof of efficacy in humans is pending, and dedicated randomized controlled trials with arrhythmia endpoints are still required for clinical validation.

items.title: EPHA2 and EPHB4 expression in human brain tumors and preclinical evaluation of EPHRIN-B2-based CAR-T cells.
items.abstract: To characterize EPHA2 and EPHB4 expression in human brain tumors and evaluate the preclinical antitumor activity of EPHRIN-B2-based chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. EPHA2 and EPHB4 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry in 141 specimens from 116 patients; 113 specimens were included in analyses by histological category. EPHRIN-B2-based CAR-T cells were generated using the piggyBac transposon system. In vitro activity was evaluated against six brain tumor cell lines and a receptor-negative control line. Intracerebroventricular administration was assessed in two intracranial xenograft models, with mock T cells, control CAR-T cells, and phosphate-buffered saline as comparators. EPHA2 expression was observed across histological categories, whereas higher EPHB4 expression was predominantly found in high-grade tumors. Among glioblastoma/gliosarcoma specimens, 74% and 37% had staining scores ≥ 2 for EPHA2 and EPHB4, respectively. High expression of both receptors within the same specimen was concentrated in high-grade tumors. CAR-T cells reduced viable tumor cell numbers and increased interferon-γ and interleukin-2 secretion against all six brain tumor cell lines, whereas no significant differences were detected with the receptor-negative control. Although differences from control T cells did not reach statistical significance, EPHRIN-B2-based CAR-T cells reduced tumor signals relative to saline-treated controls at selected time points in both xenograft models. These findings characterize EPHA2 and EPHB4 expression in human brain tumors and demonstrate in vitro antitumor activity of EPHRIN-B2-based CAR-T cells, providing a basis for further studies to establish CAR-specific efficacy in intracranial tumors. REGISTRY AND THE REGISTRATION NO. N/A.

items.title: Basophil Activation Testing: From Diagnostic Adjunct to Precision Allergy Management.
items.abstract: Basophils are rare circulating granulocytes that trigger immediate hypersensitivity reactions through IgE-mediated degranulation and also contribute to innate immunity. The basophil activation test (BAT) is a flow cytometry-based functional assay that quantifies basophil reactivity and sensitivity following allergen stimulation, offering a safe, blood-based alternative to in vivo provocation testing. This review summarizes the immunological basis of the BAT, its technical requirements, and its expanding clinical applications across food, respiratory, drug, and hymenoptera venom allergies, autoimmune chronic spontaneous urticaria, and vaccine hypersensitivity. Beyond diagnosis, the BAT increasingly supports monitoring of allergen immunotherapy and biologic treatments, prediction of reaction severity and treatment response, and personalized management decisions. Its performance varies by allergen and clinical context, and wider adoption is constrained by the absence of standardized protocols, validated cut-offs, and reference materials, as well as by basophil non-releasers and dependence on fresh viable blood. Passive BAT and mast cell activation test formats extend testing to patients in whom the conventional BAT is uninterpretable. Automated, data-driven analysis and machine learning-assisted, label-free platforms offer promising routes toward more objective, scalable interpretation. With continued standardization, harmonization, and prospective validation, the BAT is positioned not only as a diagnostic adjunct but as a platform for precision-based allergy management.

items.title: Primary Mediastinal B-Cell Lymphoma in Clinical Practice: A Case-Based Approach to Unresolved Diagnostic and Therapeutic Dilemmas.
items.abstract: Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBL) is a rare and biologically distinct subtype of aggressive B-cell lymphoma that predominantly affects young adults. Despite substantial therapeutic advances, several aspects of its management remain controversial, including frontline treatment selection, the role of radiotherapy, PET-based response assessment, and the optimal sequencing of immunotherapies in relapsed disease. Drawing on prospective and retrospective studies, cooperative group data, expert consensus and our own real-world experience, we present a practical case-based approach across the disease course, built around four clinical cases followed to their resolution and covering diagnosis, frontline treatment, PET-guided response assessment, pregnancy-associated disease, adolescents and young adults, relapsed or refractory disease, and long-term follow-up. We focus on decision-making where evidence remains limited, including the integration of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), CAR-T cell therapy, radiotherapy and transplantation, and the emerging role of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and radiomics. Management increasingly relies on individualized, multidisciplinary decision-making that integrates disease biology, functional imaging and patient characteristics to maximize cure while minimizing long-term toxicity. In our practice this translates into dose-intensified frontline chemoimmunotherapy rather than R-CHOP21, omission of radiotherapy after a complete metabolic response and, where these treatments are accessible, a second-line strategy built on checkpoint inhibitors and anti-CD19 CAR-T cells, with early referral for cellular therapy in refractory or early relapse.

items.title: Extragenital Lichen Sclerosus and Granulomatous Dermatitis in a Patient Treated With Nivolumab and Ipilimumab for Malignant Melanoma: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Lichen sclerosus (LS) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease that most commonly affects the anogenital region but may also have extragenital involvement. We report a case of a 75-year-old man treated with combination nivolumab and ipilimumab immunotherapy for metastatic melanoma who developed multiple cutaneous eruptions, some sequential and some concurrent, over approximately 21 months, spanning combination therapy, an interval of roughly 10 months off immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, and subsequent single-agent nivolumab restarted for disease progression. He first developed a pruritic erythematous maculopapular eruption consistent with ICI dermatitis, followed months later, in an overlapping distribution on the back, buttock, posterior thighs, and arms, by asymptomatic round hypopigmented patches that became large annular-polycyclic atrophic plaques that later became fissured and painful at sites of pressure and friction. Punch biopsies confirmed extragenital LS in the polycyclic plaques and non-necrotizing granulomatous dermatitis in concurrent erythematous papules of the back. The patient also developed a granulomatous rosacea-like facial eruption without prior history of rosacea and a psoriasiform/eczematous palmar dermatitis. Serial fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)/computed tomography (CT) imaging demonstrated a recurring pattern of bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy that emerged with active ICI exposure, was considered by interpreting radiologists to be likely ICI-related, and is consistent with a possible concurrent thoracic sarcoid-like reaction. The LS plaques were largely recalcitrant to topical therapy; none of the agents trialed, including clobetasol propionate 0.05% ointment, tacrolimus 0.1% ointment, and ruxolitinib 1.5% cream, produced clear improvement in the lesions. During combination therapy and the ICI-free interval, the eruption improved with each course of oral prednisone and flared within weeks of every taper, whereas no topical agent produced a comparable response. The facial eruption resolved with topical metronidazole, and the palmar dermatitis improved with topical corticosteroids. At three-month follow-up, after three further cycles of single-agent nivolumab and a period of patient-directed treatment discontinuation of topical therapy at minimally symptomatic sites, the LS showed evidence of interval progression and the palmar dermatitis had worsened, while the facial eruption remained controlled. Nivolumab was then discontinued due to intolerable systemic immune-related adverse events (irAEs), and oral prednisone was restarted. In the same interval, the fissuring posterior thigh and buttock LS improved, the granulomatous papules on the back resolved, and the palmar dermatitis cleared almost completely.

items.title: Synergistic Effects of Radiotherapy and Immunotherapy in Gastrointestinal Malignancies: Biological Rationale, Clinical Evidence, and Future Directions.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers rank among the most common and lethal malignancies, and most are immunologically "cold," showing limited baseline sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Radiotherapy (RT) can boost antitumor immune responses and may convert some of these tumors into more treatment-responsive forms. This gives RT-ICI combinations a solid biological justification. However, clinical evidence supporting this approach in GI cancers remains limited relative to that in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and non-small cell lung cancer. So far, the strongest data come from esophageal/gastroesophageal junction cancer and rectal cancer. In esophageal cancer, combining PD-1 blockade with neoadjuvant or perioperative chemoradiotherapy (CRT) results in substantial pathological responses. Furthermore, adjuvant PD-1 therapy after neoadjuvant CRT and R0 resection improves disease-free survival in patients with residual disease. In rectal cancer, adding PD-1 blockade to total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) protocols increases pathological response rates and supports organ-preservation strategies. Hepatobiliary studies suggest high intrahepatic control and meaningful conversion-to-curative potential with RT-ICI, whereas pancreatic and other GI sites are represented mainly by early-phase, heterogeneous studies. RT dose, fractionation, and treated volume all significantly affect efficacy and safety across GI cancer sites. Treatment-related lymphopenia has become a significant challenge, prompting greater emphasis on lymphocyte-sparing treatment planning. Overall, RT-ICI combinations are safe and feasible, but a reliable survival advantage has not been established to date. Progress will depend on larger, well-powered randomized trials with standardized RT timing, prespecified patient-reported and functional outcomes, and biomarker strategies to identify which approaches truly improve long-term outcomes.

items.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Pregnant Women and Health Care Workers Regarding Antenatal Testing for HIV, Hepatitis B Virus, and Syphilis in Vietnam: Protocol for a Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis remains a preventable cause of fetal loss, neonatal morbidity, and long-term disability. In Vietnam (Viet Nam), although antenatal care coverage is high, gaps persist in the timing, uptake, and completion of screening and follow-up services for these infections. This study has 2 parallel population-specific objectives. Among women who recently gave birth, we will estimate completion of antenatal testing for HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis and its associated factors with study-defined optimal testing (completion of all 3 tests during the first trimester). Among health care workers (HCWs), we will assess knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices and identify professional factors associated with good practice regarding antenatal screening and MTCT prevention. This multicenter, hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from June to September 2026 in 4 provincial hospitals in northern Vietnam. Women completed an interviewer-administered questionnaire after delivery, once clinically stable and before discharge. Antenatal testing was verified from maternal records, laboratory reports, or electronic records whenever available. HCWs completed a separate anonymous self-administered questionnaire during the same study period. The 2 participant groups were not matched. The primary outcome for women is completion of all 3 antenatal tests during the first trimester (study-defined optimal testing). The primary outcome for HCWs is good practice regarding the prevention of MTCT. The minimum target sample sizes were 601 women and 601 HCWs. Data will be analyzed separately for each group. Descriptive analyses will summarize knowledge, attitudes, and practices indicators and service uptake. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance will be used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcomes. The protocol received ethics approval on February 9, 2026. The study is funded by Thai Binh University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Hung Yen, Vietnam. Recruitment was conducted from June to September 2026. As of manuscript submission, 601 patients and 601 health care workers had been recruited. Data cleaning is planned for October 2026, followed by statistical analysis from November to December 2026. Dissemination of the first study results is planned for the first quarter of 2027. The study will provide hospital-based evidence on completion of antenatal triple screening and provider practices. By prespecifying distinct outcomes for women and HCWs, the study is designed to identify actionable gaps while avoiding causal interpretation of cross-sectional associations.

items.title: Prevalence of autoimmune hepatitis in patients with Sjögren disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Sjögren disease (SjD) and autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) may coexist, but the prevalence of AIH in SjD patients is unclear. This study investigated the prevalence and association. Databases (Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, CNKI, Wanfang, CBMdisc, VIP) were searched up to November 14, 2025. Quality was assessed using NOS and JBI scales. Meta-analysis was performed with R 4.5.2 (PROSPERO: CRD420251233495). Fourteen studies (3697 SjD patients) were included. Overall prevalence of AIH in SjD was 2.55% (95% CI: 1.52%-4.26%). Prevalence varied by study type (retrospective cohort: 4.58%, cross-sectional: 1.72%, prospective cohort: 1.67%) and by country (China: 6.16%, Japan: 2.51%, Spain: 2.49%). Stratified by SjD diagnostic criteria (1993 European, 2002 AECG) and AIH scoring (1993 IAIHG), prevalence was approximately 2%. Prevalence of AIH in SjD patients varies significantly by study design and region. Early diagnosis and treatment of AIH may improve quality of life and prognosis in SjD patients. This meta-analysis provides the first pooled estimate regarding the prevalence of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) in patients with Sjögren disease (SjD): 2.55% (95% CI 1.52%-4.26%; 14 studies, 3697 patients). Subgroup analyses indicated that AIH prevalence was influenced by study design, whereas estimates stratified by SjD and AIH diagnostic criteria were of similar magnitude (approximately 2%). Regional estimates showed numerical differences, but the differences were not statistically significant; the numerically higher estimates may reflect differences in genetic susceptibility, selection bias, environmental factors, and medical screening strategies, as well as referral and detection bias. Given the observational and largely cross-sectional design of the included studies, these estimates only motivate a hypothesis-generating immunometabolic framework, rather than permitting causal or mechanistic inference. In this framework, the liver may serve as a source of autoantigens through modifications of oxidation, glycosylation, and lipidation, including the hepatocyte β2GPI-PON1 axis; this mechanism remains to be tested in the SjD-AIH overlap.

items.title: Low public awareness of hepatocellular carcinoma risk factors.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) prevention can be mediated through hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination, hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, and alcohol control. We assessed public awareness of their carcinogenic risks and association with digital information seeking behaviors. We analyzed the nationally representative 2024 Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS 7), including 6,711, 6,661, and 6,793 respondents with observed HBV, HCV, and alcohol awareness outcomes, respectively. Survey-weighted logistic regression with multiple imputation of missing covariates assessed associations with sociodemographic characteristics and digital behaviors. Overall awareness was low: only 18.0%, 16.7%, and 37.1% recognized HBV, HCV, and alcohol as carcinogenic, respectively. Older age was independently associated with lower alcohol-related awareness; compared with adults aged 18-34 years, those aged 35-49 years (aOR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93), 50-64 years (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.78), and ≥65 years (aOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.36-0.68) had lower awareness. Higher educational attainment was associated with greater alcohol-related awareness (aOR 1.86, 95% CI 1.47-2.34). Online health information seeking was associated with greater awareness of HCV-related (aOR 1.74, 95% CI 1.17-2.59) and alcohol-related cancer risk (aOR 1.95, 95% CI 1.44-2.63), but not HBV-related cancer risk (aOR 1.40, 95% CI 0.95-2.08). However, social media use was not independently associated with risk awareness in multivariable models. Public awareness of HCC risk factors remains low. General social media use was not independently associated with cancer-risk awareness, whereas online health information seeking was associated with greater HCV- and alcohol-related awareness. These findings highlight opportunities for more targeted, literacy-sensitive HCC-prevention communication. Public awareness that hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, and alcohol consumption are associated with cancer risk remains low among U.S. adults. Using nationally representative HINTS 7 data, we identified sociodemographic differences in awareness and found that general social media use was not independently associated with awareness after multivariable adjustment, whereas online health information seeking was associated with greater awareness of HCV- and alcohol-related cancer risk. These findings highlight opportunities for targeted, literacy-sensitive communication strategies that facilitate access to credible health information and strengthen HCC prevention efforts.

items.title: Comparative risk of hepatocellular carcinoma among people with chronic hepatitis B treated with tenofovir or entecavir: A population-based linkage study.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence and mortality are rising in Australia and globally. Antiviral therapies entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) are widely used to treat chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and reduce HCC risk, but uncertainty persists regarding their relative HCC prevention impact. This study characterises HCC incidence among people with CHB treated with ETV or TDF, including sub-populations recommended for HCC surveillance. We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study in New South Wales, Australia, using linked public health datasets: 10,698 people with CHB were eligible after receiving at least 12 months of stable antiviral therapy with ETV (n=7,139) or TDF (n=3,559). Follow-up occurred from 2007-2022. Crude annual incidence rates and adjusted Cox proportional hazard ratios were calculated for HCC. Median follow-up was 86.3 months, including 89.2 months and 82.3 months among participants receiving TDF and ETV, respectively. During follow-up, 300 (2.8%) participants were diagnosed with HCC, an incidence of 4.12 per 1000 person years. Participants treated with TDF had a lower hazard ratio for HCC (aHR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.46-0.82) compared to those treated with ETV. Baseline variables associated with increased HCC risk were older age (reference <50 years: 50-59 years aHR: 2.15, 95% CI: 1.45-3.18; 60-69 years aHR: 3.42, 95% CI: 2.38-4.91; 70-79 years aHR: 4.28, 95% CI: 2.89-6.34; ≥80 years aHR: 3.95, 95% CI: 2.51-6.22), male sex (aHR: 3.14; 95% CI: 2.31-4.25), alcohol use disorder (aHR: 2.33; 95% CI: 1.28-4.25), and history of decompensated cirrhosis (aHR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.27-4.07). In people with chronic hepatitis B in Australia on stable antiviral therapy hepatocellular carcinoma risk was lower among those receiving entecavir than those receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, although confounding remains a potential explanation. Comparative HCC risk between entecavir and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in chronic hepatitis B remains uncertain outside East Asian cohorts. This population-based linkage study of people with chronic hepatitis B in Australia found TDF was associated with lower HCC risk than entecavir, a finding relevant to clinicians and researchers working on HCC prevention. These results support consideration of TDF as a preferred antiviral where clinically appropriate and highlight the need for HCC screening guidelines to account for treatment status alongside established risk factors such as older age and alcohol use disorder. As treatment was not randomised and residual confounding could not be completely mitigated, further prospective studies are needed to confirm this association.

items.title: Hepatitis C Elimination in Latin America: Progress, Disparities, and Lessons for the Next Phase of Liver Health.
items.abstract: In 2016, the World Health Organization set goals to eliminate the hepatitis C virus (HCV) as a public health threat by 2030; these include a 90% reduction in new infections, a 65% reduction in HCV-related mortality, the diagnosis of 90% of infected individuals, and the treatment of 80% of those eligible. Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) make a viral cure technically achievable, progress in Latin America remains heterogeneous. In this structured narrative review and country-level policy mapping, we assess the current epidemiology of HCV, screening and diagnostic pathways, care models, access to DAAs, national guidelines, and surveillance capabilities in select Latin American countries. While formal elimination commitments are becoming more common, universal or expanded screening, reflex diagnostic pathways, decentralized care, and integrated longitudinal registries remain unevenly implemented. Persistent deficiencies are particularly relevant for people who inject drugs (PWID), incarcerated populations, migrants, and other groups with barriers to conventional care. International experience supports point-of-care and reflex testing, prison-based testing and treatment, harm reduction integration, and decentralization as strategies to close these gaps. After achieving a sustained virological response, elimination programs must also address residual fibrosis, hepatocellular carcinoma risk, metabolic and alcohol-related liver injury, and the risk of HCV reinfection in populations that remain exposed to the virus.

items.title: [Position paper: surveillance for pancreatic cancer in individuals at elevated risk for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma].
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, where treatment options are limited. Studies suggest that early detection programs for individuals with increased genetic or familial risk may enable diagnosis and surgical treatment at a potentially curable stage. Early detection programs for pancreatic cancer show effectiveness and are cost-effective in populations stratified by the appropriate age to initiate surveillance. There is no benefit in participating in such a program for individuals who are not interested in surgery or are not surgical candidates due to their medical condition. Annual surveillance with MRI or endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) is recommended for carriers of specific gene mutations-such as BRCA2, even without a family history of pancreatic cancer and for carriers of other genes only when a family history is present, or for individuals with a strong family history even without an identified genetic mutation. This position paper details surveillance recommendations for high-risk populations.

items.title: [Position paper: colonoscopy preparation - the position of the Israeli Association of Gastroenterology and Liver Diseases].
items.abstract: Preparing for a colonoscopy involves bowel cleansing and medication adjustments, including anticoagulants and anti-diabetics. Various protocols can make these adjustments confusing for both physicians and patients. While essential for a successful procedure, this preparation can cause discomfort and carry potential risks. We aimed to provide clear guidance for colonoscopy preparation, achieving consensus among multiple societies to ensure safety and effectiveness, including patient forms. This position paper is based on guidelines from major professional associations in Europe and the USA. Representatives from associations in Gastroenterology, Pharmacology, Hematology, Nephrology, Endocrinology, and Geriatrics have collaborated to develop these recommendations. Bowel preparation now requires two days using a split-dose method. Updated guidelines include "enhanced" preparation definitions, adjustments for anti-diabetic drugs, discontinuation of anticoagulants, enoxaparin bridging, and resuming therapy post-procedure. PicoLax is suitable for patients with a GFR above 30 mL/min. New glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist guidelines address gastroparesis and sedation risks. Finally, we provide breastfeeding recommendations for colonoscopy. This consensus paper provides interdisciplinary guidance to ensure effective bowel preparation while addressing safety concerns, making it a valuable resource for healthcare providers and patients.

items.title: Real-world Gastrointestinal, Pancreaticobiliary, Cardiorenal, Metabolic and Nutritional Outcomes of GLP-1 or GIP Receptors Agonists -based Therapy in Chronic Pancreatitis.
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1(GLP-1) receptor agonists and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists are increasingly used for metabolic disease, but their safety profile in patients with chronic pancreatitis (CP) remains uncertain. We compared several gastrointestinal, cardio, renal and metabolic outcomes in patients with CP exposed to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide versus propensity-matched unexposed controls. We conducted a retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX federated real-world data platform. Adults with CP were classified by recorded exposure to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide versus no recorded exposure to those drugs. Risk analyses and Kaplan-Meier time-to-event analyses were done. After matching, median follow-up was 588 (IQR 831) versus 879 (IQR 807), respectively. Nausea/vomiting occurred in 656/4,938 (risk 0.133) versus 1,099/5,585 (risk 0.197), with risk ratio (RR) 0.675 (95%CI: 0.618-0.738) and hazard ratio (HR) 0.710 (95%CI: 0.645-0.783). Bowel obstruction/ileus occurred in 241/9,103 (risk 0.026) versus 466/8,949 (risk 0.052), with RR=0.508 (95%CI: 0.436-0.592) and HR=0.556 (95%CI: 0.476-0.649). Upper gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 355/8,536 (risk 0.042) versus 608/8,657 (risk 0.070), with RR=0.592 (95%CI: 0.521-0.673) and HR=0.659 (95%CI: 0.578-0.751). Biliary/procedural outcomes were lower, including cholecystectomy (risk 0.023 vs 0.049; HR=0.486, 95%CI: 0.412-0.572) and ERCP (risk 0.026 vs 0.064; HR=0.420, 95%CI: 0.362-0.488). Recurrent acute pancreatitis occurred in 329/5,639 exposed patients (risk 0.058) versus 579/5,499 controls (risk 0.105), with HR=0.584 (95%CI: 0.510-0.669). Additional associations included lower insulin initiation (risk 0.178 vs 0.269; HR=0.731, 95%CI: 0.658-0.812), heart failure (risk 0.061 vs 0.101; HR=0.687, 95%CI: 0.613-0.770), myocardial infarction (risk 0.039 vs 0.054; HR=0.818, 95%CI: 0.712-0.939 and acute kidney injury (risk 0.086 vs 0.150; HR=0.643, 95%CI: 0.580-0.712), malnutrition (risk 0.049 vs 0.107; HR=0.491, 95%CI: 0.438-0.550). Exposure to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide was associated with lower recorded risks across several gastrointestinal, cardio, renal and metabolic outcome domains. These findings should be interpreted with caution, and further prospective studies are required to confirm the same.
items.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD

items.title: HER2-Positive Cholangiocarcinoma Following Previous Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Diagnostic Challenge and Clinical Course With Sequential Systemic Therapy.
items.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma is an aggressive malignancy associated with poor outcomes, particularly following recurrence after surgical resection. Diagnosis can be challenging when a new hepatic lesion develops in a patient with a previous malignancy. We report the case of a 54-year-old woman with a history of stage IIB cervical squamous cell carcinoma treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy and brachytherapy in 2020, who developed an indeterminate hepatic lesion in September 2021. A hepatic abscess was initially considered, but the lesion failed to respond to a full course of antibiotics. Biopsy demonstrated poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, prompting investigation for an alternative primary malignancy. Upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy were normal, and PET-CT demonstrated a solitary avid lesion in segment 8. Right hepatectomy was performed in December 2021; histology demonstrated six lesions consistent with cholangiocarcinoma, staged pT2 Nx M0, with no lymph nodes resected. Adjuvant capecitabine was commenced based on evidence from the BILCAP trial. Shortly after surgery, CT demonstrated recurrent hepatic disease, and the patient was deemed unsuitable for further surgery or liver-directed therapy. Molecular profiling demonstrated HER2 -positive, microsatellite-stable cholangiocarcinoma, with FGFR2- negative and PD-L1 CPS 0.5. Treatment for recurrent disease comprised trastuzumab with oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy, followed by trastuzumab maintenance until December 2022; gemcitabine/carboplatin for six cycles until May 2023; and FOLFIRI until August 2023. Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu) was commenced in January 2024 as a self-funded anti- HER2 treatment and discontinued in August 2024 following radiological progression. In September 2024, brain MRI demonstrated a solitary cerebral metastasis, which was treated with stereotactic radiosurgery. Palliative cisplatin was subsequently commenced. The patient died in November 2024, approximately 34 months after recurrent hepatic disease was documented. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of distinguishing a new primary intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma from metastatic disease, the role of HER2 testing in informing treatment options, and the clinical course of a patient who survived approximately 34 months after recurrent hepatic disease was documented. The observed survival does not establish a benefit attributable to any individual treatment.
authors: Nur Farah Hanee Binti Mohammad Anuar

items.title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression is Regulated by KIF4A via the HSP90-CDC37 Complex/AKT Pathway.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) seriously endangers the life and health of people all over the world, so it is necessary to further study the pathogenesis of hepatocellular carcinoma. Kinesin family member 4A (KIF4A) appears to play oncogenic roles in numerous malignancies; however, its involvement in HCC remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the biological function of KIF4A in HCC progression. Transcriptome sequencing of more than 50 HCC patient tissue samples revealed that KIF4A expression was significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and increased with clinical progression. Functional assays (CCK-8, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell) were performed following KIF4A knockdown or overexpression in SK-Hep1 and BEL-7402 cells. Downstream molecules were identified using the 4D-DIA quantitative proteomics technique and bioinformatics analysis. Additionally, in vivo experiments using subcutaneous xenograft tumor and xenograft mouse metastatic models established in immunodeficient mice confirmed that KIF4A facilitates HCC growth and metastasis. Our study provides new insights into the clinical relevance and biological function of KIF4A in HCC. We found that KIF4A was significantly elevated in liver cancer tissues and may be indicative of poor prognosis in patients. Mechanistically, our results suggest that KIF4A promotes the proliferation and metastasis of HCC cells by inhibiting the degradation of HSP90 proteasome pathway, increasing the expression of the latter in HCC, and regulating AKT phosphorylation via the HSP90-CDC37 complex. These findings provide a novel theoretical foundation for understanding the molecular mechanisms of HCC progression, as well as presents novel targets developing treatments of HCC. Our findings revealed up-regulated KIF4A expression in HCC cell lines and tissues, and may be indicative of poor prognosis in HCC patients. KIF4A mediates HCC progression by regulating the HSP90-CDC37 complex /AKT pathway.
